source.original_title: 05/02/2026 - Leonid Machitski & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/02/2026 - Leonid Machitski & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like an overview. So I've kind of got a head start anyway.' Prospect independently confirms a prior contact: 'your colleague suggested that I watch some of the videos.'

prospect.name: Leonid Machitski
prospect.location: Moscow, Russia — country house outside the city; splits time between Moscow and Los Angeles
prospect.occupation: Business owner — 'I'm very successful with my business. It doesn't take up a lot of my day-to-day time.' Former professional GT racing driver, two-time British GT champion, most recently in 2021; paused racing about four years ago.
prospect.family_status: Has several children ('I have a load of kids'); girlfriend aged 25, Russian, based between LA and Moscow
prospect.training_background: Professional athlete for the best part of 20 years. Pre-COVID trained about five times a week — weights 2-3x, cycling 2-3x, swimming 1x — and held 78 kg at roughly 11% body fat to make the 80 kg racing threshold. Currently 92-93 kg and, in his own words, barely training: half an hour of kettlebells or weights plus treadmill walking. Has used kettlebells before but never followed a kettlebell routine. Has always employed personal trainers. Dislikes running; prefers cycling.
prospect.medical: Smoker for at least 27 years; has stopped smoking but remains nicotine-dependent via vaping — 'I haven't quit vaping but I've quit smoking... I'm trying to cut this stuff off as well but I need the nicotine.' Describes himself as 'skinny fat' with a changed metabolism since COVID. No other conditions disclosed, and none were asked about.

signals: Zero price resistance, stated pre-emptively and unprompted: 'finances are not an issue, so I'm prepared to spend whatever it takes to achieve what I want'
Already buys coaching as a matter of course — 'I've had, and I always have, personal trainers, that's not an issue'
Not seeking rescue and explicitly rejects returning to his old body: 'It's not the same goal now. I don't care about my weight now. I care more about physique, how it looks, muscularity'
High self-efficacy once a system exists: 'once it's structured, I can follow it easily' — the only gap is the initial setup
Some rebuilder overlap (COVID and the war ended his athletic season) but he frames it as a new goal rather than a lost self, and carries no regret

goals.text: Get a ripped, lean athletic physique — the fighter or calisthenics look rather than a bulky powerlifting build
Rebuild muscular structure and core that he says are no longer there
Build functionality and cardio through a proper kettlebell routine
Have a structured routine he can simply follow, since the setup is the only part he procrastinates on
Stay active so the body does not go into 'grandpa mode' and hormones and everything else get harder at 43
Be in the best shape he can inside about eight months, ahead of a possible return to racing in 2027

pains.text: Never gets started — 'to the initial setup and startup of that, I just put it off until tomorrow, tomorrow, tomorrow'
Motivation died when the war stopped his racing four years ago and the external structure disappeared with it
Previous personal trainers were each too narrow — 'everybody's quite niched and tailored' — with no overall plan to hang them off
Barely training now, by his own description tickling it — half an hour of kettlebells and treadmill walking he considers a waste of time
Nicotine dependence after at least 27 years of smoking; has quit cigarettes but not vaping
Does not want to leave the house to train — the gym is five minutes away and it is still 'another reason to leave the house when I don't need to'
Metabolism changed after COVID and the muscular structure he had as an athlete is gone

objections.raw_quote: I'd like to touch on the costs and timing of start, like, the onboarding side of things, I am leaving on the 5th to Japan for a holiday for about 10 days, then I'll be traveling for a bit as well
objections.rep_response: Dissolved it logistically rather than with a play — booked the onboarding call for Monday the 4th, before departure, and framed the holiday as build time: 'whilst you're on holiday he can build everything out for you so when you get back from Japan you've got everything in line, you just have to start.'

evidence: Price stated plainly and accepted instantly: 'It's 6k for the six months.' / 'That's fine.'
Prospect had pre-empted any price objection: 'finances are not an issue, so I'm prepared to spend whatever it takes to achieve what I want'
Onboarding call agreed for a specific date — Monday the 4th — before his Japan trip on the 5th

Prospect drove the payment logistics himself: 'How do I pay? How do I pay? Because if it's by Monday, banks don't open, and we've got time difference as well' and confirmed 'I have foreign cards, so it's not an issue'
Rep began the payment flow on the call: 'I'll pull up the link for you' / 'you ready to rock and roll, and I can kind of start on this?' / 'Yeah.'

Counter-evidence: the recording is cut at that exact point — 'Let me just remove the note taker here' — so payment confirmation is not in evidence and the close rests on the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule
outcome.next_step: Payment link processed on the call; onboarding call with Trevor booked for Monday the 4th; Trevor to build the full plan while the prospect is in Japan.

notable.note: A $6,000 close in 25 minutes with no health question asked at any point — not age, not injuries, not conditions, not sleep, not energy. The one health disclosure the prospect volunteered, 27 years of smoking and continuing nicotine dependence, was waved off. Separately, the rep opened pricing with 'what's your best currency, pounds or dollars?', and on the Ad Morris call the same day the sterling number was £4,400, which is not $6,000 — the offer appears to be priced per currency rather than converted. Third occurrence in this batch of the rep stopping the recording at the payment step.

quality.notes: Persistent. Whole rep turns sit under the 'lmachitski' label — the entire 'what was it about Trevor' probe at 00:12:24 and the 'Does that align with what you're looking for?' check at 00:16:53 are the rep's. From 00:14:00 to 00:15:00 the two speakers merge into one unpunctuated block covering the calisthenics answer and the smoking disclosure. One passage at 00:23:00 appears partially redacted around a drugs reference. All roles read from content.
